METHOD / THE SHORT-CUT

A simple method. Explicit assumptions.

01—03
01

Compare additional earnings

Use the difference in median annual earnings between completers and the alternative. Compare undergraduate programs with state high school graduates; compare graduate programs with a selected bachelor’s program or your own earnings assumption.

ΔY = Ydegree − Yalternative
02

Account for costs and time

Add forgone earnings during study to additional out-of-pocket costs, such as tuition. Adjust those costs for grants and any additional living expenses.

K = s × (Yalternative − Ystudy + C)
03

Compare the shortcut with IRR

The shortcut divides the first year’s additional earnings by total investment. IRR is the rate at which the present values of all annual net cash flows sum to zero.

rshortcut = ΔY / K
Assumptions, data coverage, and cash-flow timing
  • Overall uses the official institution-wide median (MD_EARN_WNE_4YR) for federally aided undergraduate completers across all fields and undergraduate credentials. It is not an average of program medians and does not represent a particular credential or graduate degree. Program selections use EARN_MDN_4YR for the selected field and credential.
  • Earnings are medians, not means. These scenarios extend the original mean-based formula in Patrinos & Psacharopoulos (2023) using medians and out-of-pocket costs.
  • Scorecard earnings cover federally aided completers who have earnings and are not enrolled. They do not represent average outcomes for all students or all graduates. The calculation excludes the risks of dropping out or not working.
  • Arkansas refers to the institution’s location. Completers’ earnings are not limited to employment in Arkansas. Comparisons with state high school graduates retain differences in age, field of study, occupation, location, selection, and other factors.
  • The earnings gap four years after completion stands in for the gap from the first year after completion onward. The alternative’s earnings also stand in for earnings forgone during study. This is neither a guarantee of future earnings nor a causal estimate.
  • Costs occur annually from t = 0 through s − 1; earnings gaps occur annually from t = s through s + n − 1. The first benefit arrives one year after the last study cost. Terminal value after the working period is zero.
  • Costs and earnings use real dollars from the same base year. Growth and discount rates are also real. Taxes, loan interest, and social externalities are excluded. Loan principal is not added to tuition because doing so would double count costs.
  • Initial undergraduate cost assumptions use institution-level in-state tuition as a reference, not actual program-specific costs. Enter your own graduate costs. Default study durations are assumptions, not observed times to completion. Overall defaults use the institution’s predominant undergraduate credential when reported (one, two, or four years); otherwise they use four years. Adjust this to your intended path.
  • IRR is shown only when it is uniquely defined. It may be unavailable when the earnings gap or net investment is zero or negative, among other cases. Review NPV and annual cash flows alongside it.
  • Multiple campuses sharing an OPEID6 may report the same aggregated program earnings. This site does not pool them as independent samples.
